title: Coherence of outputwise operadic mapping comparisons
statement: Use the quasicategories, mapping spaces, symmetric infinity-operads, and transport frames of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], [lem-coef-relative-operadic-terminal-active-mapping], and [def-coef-colored-operator-systems]. Let $O$ be a small ordinary symmetric colored operad, allowing nullary operations, and let $B=N(O^\otimes)$ be its operator nerve, with finite tuples of colors as objects and an operation for each non-basepoint output of an arrow. Let $q:E^\otimes\to B$ be a cocartesian fibration and a map of symmetric infinity-operads. Suppose actual inert projection transports identify every tuple fiber $E_{\mathbf c}$ with $\prod_i E_{c_i}$, including the empty tuple. Fix a coherent transport frame, with operation transports $T_\theta$ and their cocartesian lift triangles. For an operator $f:\mathbf c\to\mathbf d$ and $X\in E_{\mathbf c}$, $Y\in E_{\mathbf d}$, let $M_f(X,Y)=\operatorname{hofib}_f(\operatorname{Map}_{E^\otimes}(X,Y)\to\operatorname{Map}_B(\mathbf c,\mathbf d))$. Use the comparison of [lem-coef-relative-operadic-output-mapping] from this space to the product, over outputs $j$, of $\operatorname{Map}_{E_{d_j}}(T_{\theta_j}((x_i)_{f(i)=j}),y_j)$, where $x_i,y_j$ are the inert projections of $X,Y$ and $\theta_j$ is the output operation of $f$. The outputwise comparisons are natural under restriction to an output and under coherent parameters in $X$ and $Y$. For composable operators $f:\mathbf c\to\mathbf d$ and $g:\mathbf d\to\mathbf e$, the comparison for $g\circ f$ identifies total composition in $M_f$ and $M_g$ with outputwise substitution of the corresponding operation arrows, using the composition triangles of the transport frame. These identifications include all higher simplices and are compatible with further substitution, identities, permutations, nullary input blocks, and the empty target product. Thus the comparisons form one complete coherent comparison system, rather than unrelated equivalences of individual mapping spaces; no limits or colimits in color fibers are used.

source.place: Higher Algebra (2017), Construction 2.1.1.7, Definition 2.1.1.10(2), Proposition 2.1.2.22 and Remark 2.1.3.4; naturality and substitution-coherence clause of the relative operadic Segal mapping calculation. Read online; WANTED archive in literature/. No Stacks tag states this infinity-operadic assertion.

proof.text: Work in a containing universe so that all the tuple fibers and their diagrams are small. Write $F(\mathbf c)=E_{\mathbf c}$ and $F(f)=f_!$ for the coherent transport functor supplied by [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening]. Use its classification equivalence to identify transports with the fixed frame of [def-coef-colored-operator-systems], retaining the lift triangles. Let $\lambda_{f,X}:X\to f_!X$ denote that lift. The horn and mapping-space meanings of cocartesianness agree by [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion]. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-cocartesian-transport] with $K=\Delta^0$ to obtain the equivalence $\operatorname{Map}_{E_{\mathbf d}}(f_!X,Y)\to M_f(X,Y)$ given by $u\mapsto u\lambda_{f,X}$. Use the same lemma for general $K$ whenever the objects, lifts or factorization triangles vary in a coherent parameter. Thus factorization below means this equivalence of spaces with its triangles, rather than a choice of factorization for each individual edge.

source.place: HTT Theorem 3.2.0.1 and Proposition 4.2.4.4; Propositions 2.4.4.2, 2.4.4.3 and 3.1.2.1, cocartesian duals; agent assembly

proof.text:
For output $j$ let $I_j=\{i:\bar f(i)=j\}$, let $r_j:\mathbf c\to\mathbf c|_{I_j}$ be the inert input restriction and let $\pi_j:\mathbf d\to d_j$ be the inert output projection. In the operator category $\pi_jf=\theta_jr_j$. Apply the one coherent transport functor of [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening] to these equal composites. Together with the frame's Segal identifications this gives a natural equivalence
$$a_{f,j}:T_{\theta_j}((x_i)_{i\in I_j})\xrightarrow{\sim}(\pi_j)_!f_!X.$$
Its orientation is chosen so that its lift triangle compares the two cocartesian composites from $X$ over $\pi_jf$. Consequently, if $u:f_!X\to Y$ corresponds to $\alpha\in M_f(X,Y)$, the $j$th output comparison is
$$C_f(\alpha)_j=(\pi_j)_!(u)\,a_{f,j}.$$
Indeed, precomposing this expression with the lift of $\theta_jr_j$ gives the inert projection of $u\lambda_{f,X}$. This is exactly the postcomposition-and-factorization comparison specified in [lem-coef-relative-operadic-output-mapping], which also supplies its equivalence property. The equality of base composites and the input blocks use the operator and pruning coordinates of [def-coef-colored-operator-systems]; there is no operation on inputs discarded by $f$.

source.place: Construction 2.1.1.7(2)-(3), Definition 2.1.1.10(2), Remark 2.1.2.16; agent formula for the given comparison

proof.text: The formula of step 2 is coherent in both variables. The lift is a coherent transformation, each projection transport is a functor, and $a_{f,j}$ is an equivalence of functors coming from the fixed base diagram. The coherent Hom bifunctor and its natural transformation for a functor in [lem-coef-infinity-hom-bifunctor-functoriality] therefore make postcomposition, precomposition, and application of these projection functors natural on mapping spaces. Factorization is the natural mapping-fiber equivalence of [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-cocartesian-transport]. All constructions are thus made on coherent diagrams. For a further inert restriction retaining a subset $J$ of outputs, the component formula retains exactly $j\in J$: both procedures restrict to the same composite base diagrams and their lift triangles. In the coordinates of [def-coef-colored-operator-systems], iterated restriction is precomposition by the composite simplicial map. This proves output-restriction compatibility, including its parameter restrictions; the objectwise equivalence itself is [lem-coef-relative-operadic-output-mapping].

source.place: Definition 2.1.1.10(2), Remark 2.1.3.4; coherent naturality from the cited Hom and pointwise-transport statements

proof.text:
Let $\alpha:X\to Y$ lie over $f$ and $\beta:Y\to Z$ over $g$, and write their vertical factors as $u:f_!X\to Y$, $v:g_!Y\to Z$. Denote by $\chi_{g,f,X}:(gf)_!X\xrightarrow{\sim}g_!f_!X$ the composition equivalence, oriented so that
$$\chi_{g,f,X}\lambda_{gf,X}\simeq\lambda_{g,f_!X}\lambda_{f,X}.$$
Its coherent existence is part of the transport functor and fixed lift frame in [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening] and [def-coef-colored-operator-systems]. Naturality of the coherent lift of $g$ gives $g_!(u)\lambda_{g,f_!X}\simeq\lambda_{g,Y}u$. Pasting these specified triangles gives
$$(v\,g_!(u)\,\chi_{g,f,X})\lambda_{gf,X}\simeq v\lambda_{g,Y}u\lambda_{f,X}\simeq\beta\alpha.$$
Thus the vertical factor of total composition is $v\,g_!(u)\,\chi_{g,f,X}$. This identification holds on the whole mapping spaces and on parameterized triangles: [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-cocartesian-transport] explicitly makes successive transports compatible with its precomposition equivalences. No cancellation of homotopy classes is substituted for this space-level equivalence.

source.place: HTT Propositions 2.4.1.7, 2.4.4.2 and 3.1.2.1, cocartesian duals; explicit pasting calculation

proof.text:
Fix an output $l$ of $g$, put $J_l=\{j:\bar g(j)=l\}$ and let $\psi_l$ be its operation. Its input colors are precisely $(d_j)_{j\in J_l}$. The $l$th operation of $gf$ is $\omega_l=\psi_l\circ(\theta_j)_{j\in J_l}$ with external inputs $\coprod_{j\in J_l}I_j$, ordered using the given symmetric operator presentation. Put $u_j=C_f(\alpha)_j$ and $v_l=C_g(\beta)_l$. Apply the inert restriction to $J_l$ to the pasted diagram in step 4, then its output projection to $e_l$. The two base factorizations are now exactly the two-level rooted tree with vertices $\psi_l,\theta_j$ and its contracted tree $\omega_l$. Their image under the same transport functor gives the frame comparison
$$\chi_l:T_{\omega_l}((x_i)_{i\in\coprod I_j})\xrightarrow{\sim}T_{\psi_l}((T_{\theta_j}((x_i)_{i\in I_j}))_{j\in J_l}).$$
Using step 2 on each restricted lift triangle, the displayed vertical factor in step 4 becomes
$$C_{gf}(\beta\alpha)_l\simeq v_l\circ T_{\psi_l}((u_j)_{j\in J_l})\circ\chi_l.$$
Here the middle arrow is application of the operation transport functor to the tuple of vertical arrows; the first arrow is $v_l$. Every comparison in this calculation is obtained by applying [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening] to those base diagrams and using the lift triangles of [def-coef-colored-operator-systems]. Compatibility of factorization with the pasted transports is [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-cocartesian-transport]; the identification with $C_{gf}$ is [lem-coef-relative-operadic-output-mapping]. This proves the required substitution formula, including the actual direction of its comparison.

source.place: Construction 2.1.1.7(3), Remark 2.1.2.16; agent output restriction of the preceding triangle calculation

proof.text: Retain all the simplices in these diagrams. For a chain $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ the nerve $B$ contains its $r$-simplex, whose inner faces compose adjacent operators and whose degeneracies insert identities. Apply the single coherent transport functor of [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening] to that simplex and to its inert-pruning diagrams. The resulting composition equivalences, naturality diagrams and higher homotopies restrict to exactly the ones used in steps 2, 4 and 5; they were not chosen separately for each pair. The frame of [def-coef-colored-operator-systems] keeps those lift and pruning faces. For any additional simplicial parameter $K$, use the exponentiated fibration and natural factorization equivalence of [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-cocartesian-transport] to carry the same lift diagrams to target-fiber diagrams. A face or degeneracy $K'\to K$ is literal precomposition, as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], so the pasted factorization diagrams restrict to their previous faces. Likewise, contracting a different edge of the base chain restricts the same coherent transport diagram. Hence the two iterated substitutions for three arrows are joined by its specified higher simplex, and every further chain supplies the higher compatibility by the identical restriction rule. This argument inherits the existing coherent transport and factorization diagrams; it does not infer coherent choices from unrelated equivalences of spaces. It proves all higher parameter and further-substitution clauses.

source.place: Remark 2.1.3.4 and HTT Proposition 3.1.2.1, dual; agent restriction of coherent transport diagrams in every degree

proof.text: For identities the base diagrams are degeneracies, so step 6 gives the unit comparisons of the transport frame. A permutation of a tuple is an invertible inert operator; projection after that operator is projection to the relabeled entry. The formula of step 2 therefore just relabels the factors, and applying the same transport functor to composites of permutations supplies their compatibility with substitution. These are substitutions and restrictions of the same operator diagrams of [def-coef-colored-operator-systems], with coherence supplied by [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening]. Thus neither extra orderings nor independently chosen symmetry comparisons enter the system.

source.place: Construction 2.1.1.7, identity and symmetric-operator diagrams; degeneracies in the preceding step

proof.text: If $I_j$ is empty, its restriction is to the empty tuple and $T_{\theta_j}$ is still the nullary operation transport. The comparison in [lem-coef-relative-operadic-output-mapping] retains that factor. In step 5 the input union may be empty even when $J_l$ is nonempty; the same formula then substitutes constants into $\psi_l$. If $J_l$ is empty, $\omega_l=\psi_l$ is nullary and $T_{\psi_l}$ is applied to the unique empty tuple of arrows. If the target tuple itself is empty there is no output $l$; the cited output-mapping lemma says both $M_f$ and its output product are contractible. The unique map to the empty product is compatible with every preceding restriction and composite. These checks also cover an empty set of colors. No construction above requires limits or colimits in any color fiber: the products used are the given inert Segal products, products of spaces in the comparison, and tuples serving as domains of operation transports.

source.place: Construction 2.1.1.7 with zero arity; Remark 2.1.2.16 and the empty-product clauses of the cited nodes
